common_ground: Financial proof: 500,000 THB minimum (cited variously as ~$14,500-$17,000 USD / ~EUR 13,800); for the Muay Thai route must be in a personal savings/checking account only (no investment, corporate, or crypto accounts)
Validity: 5-year, multiple-entry visa; 180 days per entry, extendable +180 days at the Immigration Bureau
Two route types: Workcation (digital nomad/remote work for foreign employer/clients) and Thai Soft Power (Muay Thai, Thai cooking, sports, medical treatment, seminars, festivals)
All foreign nationalities eligible; applicant must be 20+ with clean immigration/criminal record
Must apply from OUTSIDE Thailand (home country or nearby e.g. Vietnam/Laos/Malaysia) via the thaievisa.go.th e-Visa portal

Core documents: passport biodata page, recent passport photo, bank statements showing 500k THB with applicant's name, proof of current residence, and (soft-power) a letter of acceptance/enrollment from the institution/gym
Family/dependents: legal spouse and children under 20 can be added (proof of relationship via marriage/birth certificates), no fixed number limit
Fees: ~$275-$1,150 USD by country (~EUR 350 in Europe, ~10,000 THB); extension fee ~1,900 THB

Soft-power Muay Thai specifics (from camp-level sources): program must be MINIMUM 6 months, enrollment letter must state 6+ months, ~99% rejection for 1-month courses, gym must be government-certified
No Thai work permit allowed; remote work only for foreign employers/clients
Tax note: 180+ days in-country triggers Thai tax residency
weakness: Top organic results barely cover the soft-power Muay Thai route in operational detail (the 6-month enrollment-letter rule and government-certified-gym requirement appear only on the niche camp result at #5, not in the high-authority results)
Generic guides bury or omit the #1 cause of rejection: booking a short (1-month) course instead of a 6+ month program
Almost no result walks through an ACTUAL Muay Thai DTV application start-to-finish from the gym/camp's side (what letter the gym issues, what enrollment proof looks like)
Vague, conflicting processing timelines and fee figures across sources
Law-firm pages optimize for conversion over lived how-to detail; tax-focused blog over-indexes on US tax and under-serves the Muay Thai applicant
No interactive eligibility checker or document checklist tailored to the soft-power applicant
common_ground_note: Figures above are aggregated verbatim from competitor pages for the content brief.

gap.description: Every ranking page treats DTV as a generic digital-nomad/remote-work visa and relegates the Muay Thai soft-power route to a bullet point. None of the high-authority results (official, law firm, tax blog) explain the make-or-break operational rules of the soft-power route: the mandatory 6+ month training program, the government-certified-gym requirement, the exact enrollment/acceptance letter a camp must issue, and why 1-month courses get ~99% rejected. There is no first-hand, gym-side walkthrough of preparing a successful Muay Thai DTV application, and no soft-power-specific document checklist or eligibility tool.

recommended_angle: Position /dtv-visa/eligibility as the only DTV requirements page written by the camp that actually files Muay Thai soft-power applications: lead with the exact eligibility + document checklist for the Muay Thai route (6-month enrollment letter, government-certified gym, 500k THB in a personal account), surface the 1-month-course rejection trap competitors omit, and back every requirement with first-hand 'we prepare your acceptance letter and walk you through the e-Visa portal' experience to win E-E-A-T the generic law-firm and tax blogs cannot match.
